summary: Executable ABI-2 core ownership, status, allocator, context, handle, diagnostic, cancellation, budget, transport, shared-memory, registry, catalogue, manifest, authorization, and Linux native-worker facilities coexist with the ABI-v1 compatibility profile. Native activation fails closed when requested isolation cannot be installed. Kernel sealing, catalogue sizes above 64 entries, and WASM execution remain explicit unsupported paths.

facilities.subset: ABI negotiation; extensible descriptors; copied allocator and host tables; context-owned buffers; generation-checked handles; immutable source identities and spans; diagnostics; deterministic budgets; monotonic cancellation deadlines; bounded serialization, transport, and shared memory

ABI-v1 compatibility registration plus transactional ABI-v2 batches with semantic-version dependencies, deterministic ordering, capability intersection, initialization, reverse compensation, immutable snapshots, and stale-view rejection

deep-copied declarative entries and exact bounded MuLIB CDD resolution, including distinct invalid, duplicate, missing, conflict, unsatisfiable, limit, and callback outcomes and non-optimal LIMIT incumbents
unsupported: catalogues above 64 entries require a future dynamic-bitset planner profile

facilities.subset: inert manifest discovery; SHA-256 image authorization; host trust callback; capability-scoped host tables; bounded protocol-2 control frames; digest-checked input and staged output mappings; Linux worker isolation before executable loading; fail-closed activation
unsupported: WASM execution until an engine and enforcement adapter exists
kernel-sealed shared-memory claims for the current System V mapping transport
